title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: Britain's adopted national dish
excerpt: Tender marinated chicken in a rich, mildly spiced tomato and cream sauce. Whether invented in Glasgow or Birmingham, chicken tikka masala is undeniably British and is one of the most popular dishes in the country for good reason.
sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is widely believed to have been created in Britain in the mid to late twentieth century, adapted from South Asian cooking traditions by Indian restaurant chefs to suit British palates. Its exact origin is disputed between several cities, but its status as a British institution is not.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. An excellent batch-cook option for meal prep.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken overnight for deeper flavour.

content.text: The yoghurt marinade tenderises the chicken and forms a crust when cooked at high heat; this is what gives tikka its distinctive charred, slightly smoky character. If you have a grill, finish the marinated chicken under it for the most authentic result. The sauce can be blended completely smooth or left with a little texture.
Mix the chicken chunks with the yoghurt, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp paprika, 0.25 tsp turmeric, and a good pinch of salt. Cover and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a frying pan over a high heat with a little oil. Cook the marinated chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and just cooked through. Set aside.
In the large saucepan, heat the sunflower oil over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 10 minutes until soft and deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the cumin, coriander, 2 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp paprika, and cardamom. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and 100ml water. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened and darkened.
Stir in the double cream and the cooked chicken pieces. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Taste and season. Serve scattered with fresh coriander.

items.cause: The cream was added to a very hot sauce and boiled.
items.fix: Lower heat before adding cream and stir in gently.

items.cause: It was overcooked in the pan before going into the sauce.
items.fix: Cook chicken until just done; it finishes in the sauce.

items.cause: Tinned tomatoes had a sharp acidity.
items.fix: Add a small pinch of sugar and simmer for a few more minutes.
